mission_fit.rationale: It supplies what the RX lacks: a fitted sleeping platform, a roof rack for a rooftop tent, and a body-on-frame 4WD platform. evidence.mission_note: This GX460 delivers camping capability the RX lacks: a sleeping platform, a roof rack for a tent, and body-on-frame 4WD. The build is much heavier off-road hardware than the light-camping brief calls for, and that hardware adds no value to this buyer. It fits the capability branch, but the accelerated-bridge timeline does not justify paying a modification premium or skipping a PPI.
evidence.rationale: The listing shows a 2010 GX460 Premium at a claimed 128k mi in Redwood City, with no VIN, no history report and a clean title claimed only in prose. The attached seller-written Google Doc logs a broad fluid and plug service at 104,971 mi, regular oil changes, a timing-cover/no-coolant-leak check at 119k, recent OEM front brakes and a smog pass. It is owner-authored rather than invoiced, and nothing covers the first ~105k miles. Photos confirm an extensive build: ICON Stage 4 lift, armor bumpers, a Warn winch, roof rack, swing-out carrier and a fitted sleeping platform. The log also lists a body-mount chop, Viper cut, KDSS adapters and wheels of unknown offset. Observed defects are a heavily cracked, dye-worn driver seat bottom and a torn cargo-floor carpet. All four model-critical items remain open: SAI history, KDSS leak/level after the lift, and underbody/rust are missing, and warning lights rest on seller prose. At $22,500 the asking price sits roughly 40% above the $15,637 fair-value midpoint, and the modifications carry little value for this buyer's light-camping intent.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, the Dirt Direct install/alignment invoices, tire date codes and underbody/KDSS photos, and confirm he will allow a Bay Area PPI before any deposit.
